How to spot a fake Easypaisa or JazzCash payment screenshot

A payment screenshot is not proof of payment. Anyone can edit a screenshot, reuse an old one, or send one before the payment fails. This guide is for online sellers in Pakistan who are paid by Easypaisa, JazzCash or bank transfer.

The one check that always works

Open your own Easypaisa, JazzCash or bank app, or download your statement, and look for a credit with the same amount and the same Transaction ID that the customer sent. If the money is not in your account, the order is not paid, no matter how real the screenshot looks. Every other sign below only tells you which screenshots to check first.

Warning signs of a fake or edited screenshot

  • The amount looks out of place. Digits in a different font, size, colour or spacing from the rest of the receipt, or numbers that are not lined up, are common signs of editing.
  • The Transaction ID is missing, cut off or blurry. A real receipt shows the full Transaction ID clearly. A cropped or hidden ID is a reason to hold the order.
  • The same Transaction ID appears on two orders. One payment can only pay for one order. A reused screenshot is one of the most common tricks.
  • The date or time does not fit. A receipt dated before the order was placed, or a time far away from when the customer said they paid, needs checking.
  • The receiver name or account number is wrong. Check that the payment was sent to your account, not to someone else.
  • The status is not "successful". Words such as pending, processing or failed mean the money has not reached you.
  • The screenshot is cropped, very compressed or a photo of a screen. These hide the details you need to check.
  • The customer pushes you to ship right away. Pressure such as "I already paid, please send it now" is a reason to check the statement first, not to skip it.

Why screenshots alone are risky

Editing apps and online "fake receipt" generators make a screenshot easy to change. A payment can also fail or be reversed after the screenshot was taken. Sellers on Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp often check dozens of screenshots a day, so mistakes happen when each one is checked by eye.
